title: Burst: standardize denial reason codes + surface to routing/gateway
author: Elena Popov
description: Motivation: During burst beta we’ve had multiple cases where customers/Support see generic 429/overload errors without actionable context (e.g., cap reached vs fleet safety vs cooldown). This PR standardizes a small, stable set of burst denial reason codes in the admission controller response and propagates them through routing -> gateway so we can (a) render clear customer-facing error messages, (b) expose denial breakdowns in Console and dashboards, and (c) reduce Support back-and-forth by making the denial cause inspectable. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a versioned enum `BurstDenialReason` in `common/capacity` shared types with explicit semantics and non-overlapping categories. 2) Admission controller returns `decision=DENY` with `reason_code` and optional `retry_after_ms` for retryable denials (e.g., COOLDOWN_ACTIVE / POOL_SATURATED). 3) Routing stores the reason code in request context and includes it in structured logs + trace attributes; for HTTP responses we map denial to a consistent error payload and set `x-redwood-burst-denial-reason` header for Dedicated tenants (guarded behind feature flag). 4) Gateway maps denial reason codes to a stable `error.code` string (e.g., `burst_denied_pool_saturated`) and preserves existing status codes (429 for capacity-style denials, 503 for internal admission errors/timeouts) to avoid breaking clients. 5) Add Prometheus counter `redwood_burst_denials_total{reason=...}` with strict label set; no tenant_id label to avoid cardinality blowups. 6) Tests: unit tests for mapping table, golden tests for error payloads, and an integration test that asserts determinism: same inputs -> same denial code. Backwards compatibility: Existing clients that only look at status code/message are unaffected. Header + structured field are additive and behind `burst.denial_reasons.enabled` flag default OFF until rollout. Reason code set (initial): `TENANT_BURST_DISABLED`, `TENANT_CAP_REACHED`, `MAX_BURST_RATIO_EXCEEDED`, `COOLDOWN_ACTIVE`, `POOL_SATURATED`, `FLEET_SAFETY_CAP`, `TELEMETRY_STALE`, `POLICY_EVAL_ERROR`, `ADMISSION_TIMEOUT`. Follow-ups: Console surface (ENG-4855) will use the new read API + denial breakdown; Support playbook update in ENG-4881 to align messaging and recommended retry/backoff per reason.
commits: common(capacity): add BurstDenialReason enum + docs for semantics
admission-controller: return reason_code + retry_after_ms on deny paths
routing: propagate denial reason into ctx, structured logs, trace attrs
gateway: map denial reasons to stable error.code + optional response header
metrics: add redwood_burst_denials_total{reason} and mapping tests
tests: golden payloads + integration determinism coverage
implementation_notes: Reason code mapping intentionally avoids leaking fleet-internal details beyond what customers need to act. `POOL_SATURATED` is used when the regional/hw-class burst pool has no borrowable capacity at the moment; `FLEET_SAFETY_CAP` is used when global circuit breaker / safety cap is tripped (customer action: reduce burst or retry later). `TELEMETRY_STALE` is treated as retryable with exponential backoff; we include `retry_after_ms=250` default (configurable) to reduce thundering herds. `POLICY_EVAL_ERROR` and `ADMISSION_TIMEOUT` are surfaced as 503 with `error.code=burst_admission_unavailable` and do not include a denial header to avoid misclassification. Routing fallback behavior remains unchanged: if a request is eligible for baseline dedicated capacity it will continue on baseline path; only the burst portion is denied, and the response indicates denial only when the request cannot be served within the tenant’s baseline envelope.
api_contract: When a burst request is denied, gateway responds with HTTP 429 and JSON: `{ "error": { "type": "capacity_error", "code": "burst_denied_pool_saturated", "message": "Burst capacity is temporarily unavailable (pool saturated).", "retry_after_ms": 250 } }`. Additionally, when `burst.denial_reasons.enabled=true`, gateway sets `x-redwood-burst-denial-reason: POOL_SATURATED`. Reason codes are stable identifiers intended for dashboards, support tooling, and customer troubleshooting; do not localize them.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind flag (this PR). 2) Enable in staging for Dedicated burst beta tenants. 3) Validate metrics + no header leakage for non-Dedicated traffic. 4) Enable for beta cohort by region (us-east H100 first), monitor `redwood_burst_denials_total` and 429 rate. 5) After Support playbook update, enable header + error.code mapping globally for burst-enabled Dedicated tenants.
ci_summary: Buildkite: monorepo build (pass), unit tests (pass), lint (pass), integration tests (pass, 1 retry due to flaky timing), security scan (pass).
review_conversation: Mina Haddad (routing): Can we guarantee determinism for the reason codes under telemetry lag? I’m worried about flapping between POOL_SATURATED and TELEMETRY_STALE. Elena Popov (author): Good call. Updated admission controller to prefer TELEMETRY_STALE whenever freshness window exceeded, before saturation checks. Added an integration test asserting stable reason selection with synthetic stale timestamps. Ravi Menon: Please keep status codes unchanged; clients may treat 503 differently than 429. Also, header should be behind a flag until we confirm no proxy strips/rewrites. Elena: Kept 429/503 mapping as described; added `burst.denial_reasons.enabled` gate and default OFF. Ethan Park: Enum needs to live in shared types, not service-local, so policy engine and control plane can reference it later. Elena: Moved to `common/capacity` and updated imports. Allison Grant: Metrics label `reason` is okay, but please ensure there is no tenant_id label and cap the set. Elena: Confirmed no tenant labels; reason codes are enum-backed, and metric registration rejects unknown strings. Peter Holtz: Can we add a note about retry guidance per reason (cooldown vs pool saturated)? Elena: Added `retry_after_ms` for retryable denials and documented guidance in `burst_denial_reason.md`. Approvals: Mina Haddad approved after determinism test; Ravi Menon approved after status code confirmation; Ethan Park approved with shared-types change; Allison Grant approved with label constraints; Peter Holtz approved with retry guidance.
release_notes: Internal: Admission controller now provides standardized denial reason codes and optional retry_after hints; routing/gateway can surface these for Dedicated burst debugging behind a feature flag.
